pr_title: Fix sampling bug when SSAO is using half size
pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/62881
Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/66643

There are two pieces to this PR:
1. When downsampling 5 mip levels at once, the 5th mip level was showing some artifacts which lead to invalid samples in the SSAO shader. To fix it, I have removed the invalid averaging code from the 5th mipmap computation. This code path was only hit when using both SSAO and SSIL and only one of them is using half size
2. Change the ``half_screen_pixel_size`` to be based off the full screen size / 2. This was a difficult bug to track down, but essentially when using a screen size that could not be subdivided cleanly 4 times the half res samples would drift away from their intended positions. To fix that, we base our scaling off of the full viewport size. 

This also cleans up two unreported bugs:
1. The SSAO shader was using the wrong sampler (default instead of mirror)
2. The depth linearization process was doubling the depth value. This could have led to SSAO improperly rejecting valid occlusion (i.e. appearing slightly lighter than it should).

Finally, on investigation it appears that SSIL was suffering from the same issues, it was just less obvious. So I made the changes to SSIL as well

issue_context.title: Vulkan: Strange black line artifact in SSAO when Half Size is enabled
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

d26442e709f6361af9ac755ec9291bb43f2cd69b

### System information

Windows 10, GTX 1060 6GB

### Issue description

When SSAO quality is set to above "Low (Fast)" a weird line appears directly in the middle of the screen - it seems like some visual artifact - It always appears, but when `ssao_detail` is lowered the artifact is less visible, albeit still there.

SSAO OFF
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/76781125/178143225-aa4c6c77-3b3f-4cb9-a567-bfffde426ae6.png)

SSAO on Medium
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/76781125/178143277-032f0b3a-ddcc-4b35-ae6a-03dce3d9fae1.png)

SSAO on Low
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/76781125/178143283-1a2cdc5a-38d3-4a07-8355-a6f0e14c0a04.png)


I think it doesn't show on low because Low doesn't use the detail pass in SSAO though I'm not sure.


### Steps to reproduce

Open any scene in godot. Enable SSAO in the WorldEnvironment, and if you can't see the strange line then increase Detail and Intensity of the SSAO.

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments: Yes, everything at its default settings

I can confirm this on 4.0.alpha 1b057e18f.

A similar issue occurs with SSR and possibly SSIL. This line will move around when you resize the viewport (which happens when resizing the editor window).

Turn off Half resolution, as if the height/width of half the resolution are not both integers you get issues with it.

I've experienced a similar issue in shipped games (such as Ark Survival Evolved a UE4 title where SSAO had such Lines appearing) where on settings when Screen Space Effects are using half resolution when the Screen Resolution is such that half of it doesn't return Integer values for both.

**Minimal reproduction project:** [test_ssao_half_size.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9079562/test_ssao_half_size.zip)

I can notice flickering when resizing the viewport with Half Size enabled in the Project Settings, but everything looks OK when Half Size is disabled:

### SSAO Half Size enabled (default)

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/180032/178156065-5ded9a9d-983c-40ff-8d31-1f710de166d5.mp4

### SSAO Half Size disabled

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/180032/178156068-94012856-2cf1-4989-95f0-76bb72de90b5.mp4

I don't notice a line in the middle in either though.

> Turn off Half resolution, as if the height/width of half the resolution are not both integers you get issues with it.

So I suppose the solution would be to ensure the viewport dimensions are always a multiple of 2? I suppose all common screen resolutions are multiples of 2 anyways, eg 2560x1440, 1920x1080, 1366x768... so this is a very corner case bug

See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/37995, which was rejected.

This might have been my bad :)
I think `buffer_width` and `buffer_height` are already half `full_screen_size.xy`, Seems to be we should use `1.0/buffer_width` for normal and `1.0/half_width` for `ssil_half_size`?
I might be wrong though because `buffer_width` I think is also halved if `ssil_half_size`

The problem is 1.0 / buffer_width does not equal 2.0 / screen_width

For example. If the screen is 1001 pixels wide, 2.0/ screen_width is ``0.001998001998`` while 1.0 / buffer width is ``0.001996007984`` that small difference is enough to cause an artifact when sampling the entire screen which is exactly what we see in the attached issues
